quotes.text: Stripe doesn’t guarantee any outcomes for your use of Authorization Boost features. The optimization calculations we provide are estimates.
Adaptive Acceptance uses AI to reformat payment requests based on card issuers’ preferences.
If you apply multiple optimizations to a single payment, we attribute the benefit to the one most likely responsible for approval.
However, Stripe doesn’t reconcile these estimates directly with the fees applied to your account.
The [Optimization](https://dashboard.stripe.com/optimization) page shows cost saving estimates only for domestic payments in the US and Canada, though you might also realize savings in other markets.

findings: The May 8 and November 7 captures carry the same optimization behavior, metrics, caveats and coverage across 136 lines each. The diff shows local versus remote image references, italic/heading whitespace and Markdown table normalization, without a substantive content change (diff lines 3-150; old raw lines 4-136; new raw lines 5-136). Do not infer rollout or performance change from the new capture.

The Optimization Dashboard estimates recovered payment volume, recovered payments, approval-rate increase and network cost savings for card-not-present payments; it does not guarantee outcomes (new raw lines 7-12, 105-129; old raw lines 6-11, 104-129). The report attributes a multi-feature payment to the optimization most likely responsible for approval and models counterfactual costs rather than reconciling actual fees (new raw lines 57-73).

Adaptive Acceptance alone is described as using AI to reformat requests; card account updater uses network updater services for saved card data and network tokens substitute credentials via network integrations (new raw lines 18-55; old raw lines 17-54). The current source line 13 calls all three 'AI-driven features', a baseline overstatement also repeated in wiki/concepts/stripe-authorization-boost.md line 10.

The current source's cost-savings threshold at line 27 is grounded in new raw line 121/old raw line 121, but it omits that Dashboard cost-savings estimates are shown only for domestic US and Canada payments (new raw line 89; old raw line 88), network token fees such as VDCU are excluded (new raw line 91), and inferred savings are not reconciled to actual fees (new raw line 73). It also omits the explicit non-guarantee (new raw line 12). These are material to interpreting the analytics.

Cost savings are conditional: the page frames them for IC+ pricing and Adaptive Acceptance/network tokens, not card account updater (new raw lines 10, 41-55, 67-91, 113-121). The success-rate chart is CNP-only and raw attempt rate rather than deduplicated purchase rate (new raw lines 127-132). A visible chart, saved-card update or network token is not evidence of incremental recovered revenue for a particular payment.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/analytics/optimization, the complete November guide describes the Optimization Dashboard's estimated impact of Authorization Boost on card-not-present payment attempts: Adaptive Acceptance reformats/retries selectively, card account updater refreshes saved PAN/expiry through networks, and network tokens replace card numbers (new raw lines 10-55). Recovery is probabilistic and attributed to one most likely feature, while IC+ network cost savings are counterfactual estimates rather than account-fee reconciliation (new raw lines 57-73). The matched May 8 guide says the same (old raw lines 9-72); source-stripe-payments-optimization.md summarizes the three features and calculation at current source lines 11-27, but overcalls all three AI-driven and omits the no-guarantee, domestic US/Canada display limit and raw CNP rate boundary.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/analytics/optimization, there is no substantive behavioral change between the May 8 and November 7 captures: image paths, italics, heading whitespace and table formatting account for the diff (old raw lines 4-136; new raw lines 5-136). source-stripe-payments-optimization.md should retain May 8 local assets and historical details, add November provenance, and correct its baseline AI generalization (current source line 13; old raw lines 17-54; new raw lines 18-55). It must warn that calculations are estimates with no guaranteed outcome, savings are not reconciled to account fees or inclusive of token fees, cost estimates display only for domestic US/Canada, and success rate is a raw CNP attempt rate (old raw lines 11, 72, 88-90, 121, 127-132; new raw lines 12, 73, 89-91, 121, 127-132). No chart or feature description proves merchant eligibility, payment success or realized savings.
